description: Pyomo is an open-source, Python-based optimisation modelling language for formulating, solving and analysing optimisation models. It supports linear, quadratic and nonlinear programming, their mixed-integer variants, stochastic programming, differential algebraic equations and constraint programming, and passes models to external solvers. It was developed at Sandia National Laboratories, moved to GitHub in June 2016 and is a COIN-OR project with a development team that meets weekly. It is general-purpose and used worldwide in process systems engineering, energy system planning, water and supply chain optimisation. The code is free under the BSD licence, installed with pip, and tested on CPython 3.10 to 3.14 and PyPy 3.11, with documentation, examples and community support through a forum and StackOverflow. Caveats: Pyomo is a modelling layer, so realistic problems need a suitable solver, some of which are commercial, and large nonlinear models can be slow to build in Python. For simulation it is used to write capacity expansion, scheduling and network design models for plants, supply chains and infrastructure systems, including resilience-oriented optimisation of investment and recovery. It is related to the GEMPACK record in this catalogue, which solves equilibrium, not optimisation models.
